docs.text: Welcome to BlocKIT - a complete Unity asset for creating Block Blast style games! 🎮

docs.title: What is BlocKIT?
docs.text:
BlocKIT is a complete system for building Block Blast puzzle games. It includes everything you need:

  • 🎯 Ready-made game mechanics - drag & drop blocks on an 8x8 board
  • 🧠 Smart difficulty system - the game adapts to player skill
  • ✨ Visual effects - animations and player feedback
  • 🎵 Sound system - ready to connect your own sounds
  • 📊 Scoring system - combos, streaks, bonuses
  • 📱 Ad support - easy integration with ad networks

docs.title: Who is this for?
docs.text: ✅ Perfect for you if: - You're creating your first mobile game - You want to quickly launch a Block Blast style game - You need a working system without diving into code - You want to modify mechanics for your needs

docs.title: What is BlocKIT?
docs.text: BlocKIT is a complete Unity asset for creating Block Blast style puzzle games. It includes all core mechanics, UI, animations, and systems needed to launch a game.

docs.title: Do I need programming knowledge?
docs.text:
Basic usage: No! Most customization can be done through Unity Inspector.

Advanced features: Some C# knowledge helps for deeper modifications.

docs.title: What Unity version do I need?
docs.text:
Minimum: Unity 2021.3 LTS

Recommended: Unity 2022.3 LTS or newer

docs.title: What dependencies are required?
docs.text:
Required: - DOTween (free from Asset Store)

Optional: - TextMeshPro (for better text) - Ad SDK of your choice (AdMob, Unity Ads, etc.)

docs.title: Game won't start - what to do?
docs.text:
1. ✅ Check DOTween is installed
  2. ✅ Check NewManager exists in scene
  3. ✅ Check all references in NewManager are set
  4. ✅ Look for errors in Console

docs.title: Shapes not dragging - what's wrong?
docs.text:
1. ✅ Canvas must have GraphicRaycaster
  2. ✅ EventSystem must exist in scene
  3. ✅ NewDraggableShape needs EventTrigger component
  4. ✅ Check Camera is set in Canvas

docs.title: No animations playing - why?
docs.text:
1. ✅ Install DOTween from Asset Store
  2. ✅ Restart Unity after DOTween installation
  3. ✅ Check using DG.Tweening; in scripts
  4. ✅ Verify DOTween setup ran successfully

docs.title: Game is laggy on mobile - how to optimize?
docs.text:
1. Reduce board size: 8×8 → 6×6
  2. Disable particles: Set particlesEnabled = false
  3. Simplify animations: Increase duration constants
  4. Lower quality: Edit → Project Settings → Quality
  5. Optimize sprites: Use sprite atlas, compress textures

docs.text:
Balance: - Base points: Small (3-5 per shape) - Line clear: Medium (100-200) - Combo: Large multiplier (1.5x - 3.0x)

Psychology: - Players love big combo numbers! - Frequent small wins keep engagement - Rare huge scores create "wow" moments

Hardcore: 10-30 minutes

docs.title: Success Score Calculation
docs.text:
float CalculateSuccessScore()
{
    float score = 0f;

    // Lines cleared (0.0 - 1.0)
    score += (linesCleared / maxPossibleLines) * 0.4f;

    // Combo bonus (0.0 - 1.0)
    score += (comboLength / 10f) * 0.3f;

    // Efficiency (0.0 - 1.0)
    score += (shapesUsedWell / totalShapes) * 0.3f;

    return Mathf.Clamp01(score);
}

docs.title: Board State Analysis
docs.text:
Brain considers current board:

float AnalyzeBoardDifficulty()
{
    // How full is board? (0.0 - 1.0)
    float fillPercentage = FilledCells / TotalCells;

    // How fragmented? (0.0 - 1.0)
    float fragmentation = CalculateFragmentation();

    // How many valid placements? (0.0 - 1.0)
    float validSpaces = CountValidSpaces() / TotalCells;

    return (fillPercentage + fragmentation - validSpaces) / 3f;
}

float CustomDifficultyCurve(int turnsPlayed)
{
    // Easy for first 50 turns
    if (turnsPlayed < 50)
        return 0.3f;

    // Gradually increase
    float progress = (turnsPlayed - 50) / 200f;
    return Mathf.Lerp(0.3f, 0.8f, progress);
}

docs.title: Changing Board Colors/Board Size
docs.text: The board uses a single texture image containing a full 9×9 grid. Each square in the image has a fixed pixel size that must match the CellSize value in the NewMatrix component.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The board is rendered using one image, not individual cell sprites
  • The image contains 9×9 drawn squares
  • The pixel size of each square in the image must be exactly the same as the CellSize value in NewMatrix
  • Board colors are defined directly in the image, not in the Inspector

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:

  2. Make sure each square is exactly the same pixel size as CellSize in the NewMatrix Inspector
  3. Change the colors or style of the squares as needed
  4. Save the image and return to Unity — the board will update automatically

docs.title: Example: Creating an 8×8 Board
docs.text:
1. Open the board image in a graphic editor
  2. Draw an 8×8 grid instead of 9×9
  3. Increase the size of each square so the board fills the screen correctly (for example, each square may be 110×110 pixels)
  4. Set CellSize in the NewMatrix Inspector to 110
  5. Make sure the grid is centered in the image
  6. Save the image and return to Unity
  7. In Unity, open the Prefabs folder and select GridCell, then set its Width and Height to match the CellSize value in NewMatrix (Inspector). This value represents the size of a single cell — one block unit that the shapes are built from.

The board will automatically align correctly as long as: - the number of squares in the image matches the intended grid size - the pixel size of each square matches the CellSize value

docs.title: How does Block Blast work?
docs.text:
Block Blast is a simple but addictive puzzle game:

  1. You get 3 random blocks of different shapes
  2. Place them on an 8x8 board by dragging and dropping
  3. Fill complete lines (horizontal or vertical)
  4. Filled lines disappear and you get points
  5. Game ends when there's no space for any block

docs.title: Board (Matrix)
docs.text:
• Grid of 8 rows × 8 columns = 64 cells
  • Each cell can be empty or occupied
  • When an entire row or column is occupied → line clears

docs.title: Blocks (Shapes)
docs.text:
• Small arrangements of colored squares
  • From 1 to 9 squares in different configurations
  • Player gets 3 random blocks per turn
  • When all 3 are used → new turn with next 3 blocks

docs.title: Combo
docs.text:
• When you clear multiple lines at once = COMBO!
  • More lines → more points
  • Combo multiplies points and gives bonus

docs.title: Ghost Preview
docs.text:
• When you drag a block over the board
  • Shows where the block will appear if you drop it
  • Helps player plan moves

docs.title: How does it work in Unity?
docs.text:
BlocKIT consists of several main systems:

NewManager (boss of everything)
    ├── NewMatrix (board)
    ├── NewShapeSpawner (generates blocks)
    ├── NewBrain (AI - difficulty)
    ├── NewScoreManager (scoring)
    └── SoundManager (sounds)

docs.title: Game Flow
docs.text:
Start Game
    ↓
Generate 3 blocks
    ↓
Player drags block ──→ Can place? ──→ No ──→ Try again
    ↓ Yes
Place on board
    ↓
Check lines ──→ Full lines? ──→ Yes ──→ Clear lines + points
    ↓ No                              ↓
All 3 used? ──→ No ──→ Wait          ↓
    ↓ Yes                             ↓
Can place new blocks? ──→ Yes ──→ Generate 3 blocks
    ↓ No
GAME OVER

docs.title: 1. Placing Blocks
docs.text:
• Block must fully fit on the board
  • Cannot place on occupied cells
  • Once dropped → sticks immediately

docs.title: 2. Clearing Lines
docs.text:
• System checks after each move
  • Clears all full lines at once
  • Both horizontal and vertical

docs.title: 3. Game Over
docs.text:
• When none of the 3 blocks fit on the board
  • Game shows popup with score
  • Can play again

docs.title: Game Logic - How Decisions Are Made
What is NewBlockBlastLogic?
docs.text:
NewBlockBlastLogic is the intelligent system that picks which shapes to give you. It's not random - it's smart!

Goal: Keep game challenging but not impossible.

docs.title: Why do we need smart logic?
Without smart logic (pure random):
docs.text:
Game gives: [huge L] [huge T] [huge Z]
Board: 90% full
Result: INSTANT GAME OVER 😢

docs.title: With smart logic:
docs.text:
Game gives: [small line] [single] [medium square]
Board: 90% full
Result: Player can clear lines and continue! 😊

docs.title: The 3-Step System
docs.text:
Step 1: Try to find COMBO shape
   ↓ Found?
   Yes → Give it + 2 balanced shapes
   No → Go to Step 2
   ↓
Step 2: Try to find NEAR-MISS shape
   ↓ Found?
   Yes → Give it + 2 balanced shapes
   No → Go to Step 3
   ↓
Step 3: Give 3 SAFE shapes
   (Always fit somewhere)

docs.title: What are these shape types?
docs.text: Type Description Example COMBO Instantly completes a line Line that fills last 3 cells in row NEAR-MISS Almost completes line (1-2 cells missing) Would complete if 1 more piece placed SAFE Small, always fits somewhere Single cell, small 2×2 square

docs.title: Early Game (Board <50% full)
docs.text:
Give: Mostly medium/large shapes
Why: Player has space, can handle bigger pieces
Effect: Faster scoring, more freedom

docs.title: Mid Game (Board 50-75% full)
docs.text:
Give: Mix of sizes
- 1 combo/near-miss opportunity
- 1 medium shape
- 1 small/safe shape
Why: Balance challenge with possibility

docs.title: Late Game (Board >75% full)
docs.text:
Give: More small shapes, higher combo chance
Why: Player needs help clearing space
Effect: Still challenging but not impossible

docs.title: 1. Find Immediate Combo
docs.text:
For each shape in pool:
  For each position on board:
    If placing shape here clears any line:
      → Return this shape! ✓

If no combo found:
  → Continue to next step

docs.title: 2. Find Near-Miss
docs.text:
For each line (row/column):
  Count empty cells
  If 1-2 empty cells:
    → This is "almost full"

For each shape:
  For each position:
    If placing shape fills almost-full line:
      → Return this shape! ✓

docs.title: 3. Safe Fallback
docs.text:
Filter shapes by:
  - Can be placed SOMEWHERE on board
  - Sorted by size (small → large)

Give mix:
  - 1 small (always fits)
  - 1 medium
  - 1 random

docs.title: Adaptive Difficulty
docs.text:
System tracks player performance:

Player clearing many combos:
   ↓
Increase difficulty
   ↓
Give fewer combo opportunities
Give larger shapes

Player struggling:
   ↓
Decrease difficulty
   ↓
Give more combo opportunities
Give smaller shapes

docs.title: Constants (Tuning Knobs)
docs.text:
These control the system:

SHAPES_PER_TURN = 3          // How many shapes per turn
MAX_MISSING_CELLS = 8        // Max empty cells in "near-miss"
HIGH_FILL_THRESHOLD = 0.76   // When board is "full" (76%)
MIN_PLAYABLE_SHAPES = 3      // Min shapes that must fit
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 150           // Max tries to find good set

docs.title: What they do
docs.text: Constant Effect if increased Effect if decreased SHAPES_PER_TURN More choices → easier Fewer choices → harder MAX_MISSING_CELLS More "near-miss" → easier Stricter matching → harder HIGH_FILL_THRESHOLD Earlier help → easier Later help → harder MIN_PLAYABLE_SHAPES Must fit more → easier Can give impossible → harder

docs.title: Almost-Full Lines
docs.text:
System detects patterns:

Full row:
■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■  ← Would clear

Almost full (1 missing):
■ ■ □ ■ ■ ■ ■ ■  ← Could give shape to fill

Almost full (2 missing):
■ □ ■ ■ ■ □ ■ ■  ← Could give shape to fill

docs.title: Smart Shape Selection
docs.text:
If missing cells are:
  Adjacent (■ ■ □ □ ■):
    → Give 2-cell line shape

  Scattered (■ □ ■ □ ■):
    → Give L or T shape

  Corners (□ ■ ■ ■ □):
    → Give corner shape

docs.title: Balance System
docs.text:
After picking priority shape, fills remaining:

Priority shape picked: Large (5 cells)
   ↓
Balance:
  Shape 2: Small (1-2 cells)
  Shape 3: Medium (3-4 cells)

Why? Ensures at least ONE shape is easy to place!

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Before giving shapes to player:

Check: Can player place at least 3 shapes?
   ↓ Yes
   Give shapes ✓
   ↓ No
   Try again (up to 150 attempts)
   ↓ Still no?
   Give 3 guaranteed-safe shapes

This prevents impossible situations!

docs.title: Logic Decision Process
docs.text:
1. Check for combo:
   → Row 0 needs 1 cell at position (0,2)
   → Found single-cell shape! ✓

2. Pick combo shape:
   Shape 1: Single cell ■

3. Balance with 2 more:
   Shape 2: 3-cell line ■ ■ ■
   Shape 3: 2×2 square ■ ■
                      ■ ■

Result: Player has combo opportunity + backup options

docs.title: Make game easier
docs.text:
// Give more combo opportunities
HIGH_FILL_THRESHOLD = 0.60f;  // Was 0.76

// Require more shapes to fit
MIN_PLAYABLE_SHAPES = 4;  // Was 3

// Allow more missing cells
MAX_MISSING_CELLS = 12;  // Was 8

docs.title: Make game harder
docs.text:
// Give fewer combo opportunities
HIGH_FILL_THRESHOLD = 0.85f;

// Can give fewer playable shapes
MIN_PLAYABLE_SHAPES = 2;

// Stricter near-miss
MAX_MISSING_CELLS = 4;

docs.title: Remove intelligence (pure random)
docs.text:
// In NewBlockBlastLogic.cs
public ShapeData[] PickTurnSet(ShapeData[] pool)
{
    // Just pick 3 random shapes
    return pool.OrderBy(x => Random.value).Take(3).ToArray();
}

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Very fast - runs in <1ms even on slow devices
  • Cached checks - board state analyzed once
  • Early exits - stops when good solution found
  • Fallback safety - always has backup plan

docs.title: What is it?
docs.text:
NewManager is the main brain of the game. It:

  • 🎮 Starts the entire game
  • 🔄 Coordinates all components
  • 📊 Tracks game state
  • 🎯 Responds to player actions

Analogy: Like an orchestra conductor - doesn't play itself, but makes everyone play together.

docs.text:

│ Matrix: [NewMatrix]              │ ← Board
│ Shape Spawner: [NewShapeSpawner] │ ← Block generator
│ Score Manager: [NewScoreManager] │ ← Points
│ Brain: [NewBrain]                │ ← AI difficulty
│ Draggable Prefab: [Prefab]       │ ← Block template

docs.text: Field What is it? Why? Matrix Reference to board Manager needs to know where the board is Shape Spawner Block generator Creates new blocks on screen Score Manager Scoring system Counts points, combos, highscore Brain Artificial intelligence Selects block difficulty Draggable Prefab Block prefab Template for creating new blocks Shape Data Assets Shape list All possible blocks in the game

docs.title: Game Start
docs.text:
1. NewManager.Awake()
   ↓
2. Initialize all components
   ↓
3. NewManager.Start()
   ↓
4. Generate first 3 blocks
   ↓
5. Wait for player input

docs.title: Game Loop
docs.text:
Player places block
   ↓
NewManager.OnShapePlaced()
   ↓
Check if lines are full
   ↓
Clear full lines (if any)
   ↓
Update score
   ↓
Check if all 3 blocks used
   ↓ Yes
Generate new 3 blocks
   ↓
Check if any block can be placed
   ↓ No
GAME OVER

docs.title: Key Methods (for programmers)
docs.text: If you want to modify code, these are the most important:

docs.title: OnShapePlaced(shape)
docs.text:
Called when player places a block on board.

// What it does:
1. Tells Matrix to add the shape
2. Checks for full lines
3. Clears lines if found
4. Updates score
5. Checks for game over

docs.title: GenerateNewShapes()
docs.text:
Creates 3 new random blocks.

// How it works:
1. Asks Brain for 3 shapes (based on difficulty)
2. Tells ShapeSpawner to create them
3. Displays them on screen

docs.title: CheckGameOver()
docs.text:
Checks if game should end.

// Checks if:
- Any of 3 blocks can fit anywhere on board
- If none fit → Game Over
- If at least one fits → Game continues

docs.title: Events You Can Listen To
docs.text:
NewManager sends events that other scripts can listen to:

Event When Use for OnGameStart Game starts Reset UI, animations OnShapePlaced Block placed Sound effects OnLinesCleared Lines cleared Visual effects OnScoreUpdated Score changes Update UI OnGameOver Game ends Show popup

docs.title: Change number of blocks per turn
docs.text:
Default is 3. To change:

// In NewManager.cs find:
private const int SHAPES_PER_TURN = 3;

// Change to whatever you want:
private const int SHAPES_PER_TURN = 5;

docs.title: Change when game is over
docs.text:
Default: game over when NO blocks fit.

Want game over when only 1 block fits?

// In CheckGameOver() change:
if (CountPlayable(currentShapes) >= 1)  // was: >= 1
    return false;  // game continues

// To:
if (CountPlayable(currentShapes) >= 2)  // now requires 2
    return false;

docs.title: Singleton Pattern
docs.text:
NewManager uses Singleton pattern - only ONE instance exists:

public static NewManager Instance { get; private set; }

This means you can access it from anywhere:

// From any script:
NewManager.Instance.GenerateNewShapes();
NewManager.Instance.CheckGameOver();

Important

Never create multiple NewManager instances! Always use Instance.

docs.text:

Think of it as a checkerboard with 64 squares, each can be empty or filled.

│ Rows: 8                          │ ← Number of rows
│ Columns: 8                       │ ← Number of columns
│ Cell Size: 60                    │ ← Size of each cell
│ Spacing: 5                       │ ← Gap between cells
│                                  │
│ Cell Prefab: [CellPrefab]       │ ← Template for cells
│                                  │

docs.text: Setting Effect Example Rows Height of board 8 = classic, 10 = harder Columns Width of board 8 = classic, 10 = harder Cell Size Pixel size of each square 60 = medium, 80 = large Spacing Gap between squares 5 = tight, 10 = loose Cell Color Empty Color when nothing there White, gray, etc Cell Color Filled Color when block placed Match your theme

docs.title: Cell Storage
docs.text:
Board stores cells in 2D array:

// cells[row, column]
cells[0, 0] = top-left cell
cells[7, 7] = bottom-right cell

docs.title: Cell States
docs.text:
Each cell can be:

  1. Empty (0) - nothing there
  2. Filled (1+) - has a block

docs.title: 1. Can Place Shape?
docs.text:
Before placing, checks if: - All shape cells fit on board (not outside) - All target cells are empty - Shape doesn't overlap existing blocks

Check each cell of shape:
  Is it inside board? ──→ No ──→ Can't place
    ↓ Yes
  Is target cell empty? ──→ No ──→ Can't place
    ↓ Yes
All checks passed ──→ Can place!

docs.title: 2. Place Shape
docs.text:
When shape is placed: 

For each cell in shape:
  1. Mark board cell as filled
  2. Update visual (change color)
  3. Add to count

docs.title: 3. Check Lines
docs.text:
After each placement: 

For each row:
  Count filled cells
  If count == 8 → Mark row for clearing

For each column:
  Count filled cells
  If count == 8 → Mark column for clearing

Clear all marked lines

docs.title: 4. Clear Lines
docs.text:
When line is full: 

1. Animate cells (fade out)
2. Set cells to empty
3. Update visuals
4. Tell ScoreManager

docs.title: CanPlaceShape(offsets, row, col)
docs.text:
Checks if shape can be placed at position.

// Returns true if:
- All cells fit inside board
- All target cells are empty

// Returns false if:
- Shape goes outside board
- Any cell already occupied

docs.title: PlaceShape(offsets, row, col)
docs.text:
Places shape on board.

// What it does:
1. For each cell in shape
2. Mark that position as filled
3. Update cell visual
4. Increment filled count

docs.title: CheckAndClearLines()
docs.text:
Finds and clears full lines.

// Process:
1. Check all rows for fullness
2. Check all columns for fullness
3. Collect full lines
4. Animate clearing
5. Reset cells to empty
6. Return count of cleared lines

docs.title: IsGameOver(shapes)
docs.text:
Checks if any shape can be placed.

// For each shape:
//   For each possible position:
//     If can place → return false (game continues)
// If no shape fits anywhere → return true (game over)

docs.title: Ghost Preview
docs.text:
When dragging a block over board:

1. Detect cursor position
2. Convert to board coordinates
3. Check if shape fits there
4. If yes → Show transparent preview
5. If no → Show red/invalid

docs.title: Cell Animations
docs.text: Different animations for: - Place - quick pop-in - Clear - fade out + scale - Highlight - pulse effect

docs.title: Change board size
docs.text:

Rows = 10;      // Make it taller
Columns = 10;   // Make it wider

// ⚠️ Warning: Must adjust UI layout!

docs.title: Custom cell colors
docs.text:
// In Inspector:
Cell Color Empty = Light Gray
Cell Color Filled = Your brand color
Cell Color Highlight = Bright color for preview

docs.title: Add cell effects
docs.text:
Want cells to glow or pulse? Modify:

void UpdateCellVisual(int row, int col)
{
    // Add your effect here
    // Example: cell.GetComponent<Glow>().Activate();
}

docs.text:
Board operations are very fast: - Placing shape: O(n) where n = cells in shape - Checking lines: O(rows + columns) = O(16) for 8×8 - Finding valid positions: O(rows × columns × shapes) but cached

No performance issues even on old devices! 📱

docs.text: BlocKIT includes a flexible ad system that works with any ad network. It's set up so you can easily plug in AdMob, Unity Ads, or any other provider.

docs.text:
Main controller for all ads.

public class AdsManager : MonoBehaviour
{
    public static AdsManager Instance { get; }

    public void ShowRewarded(Action onRewardGranted);
    public void ShowInterstitial();
    public bool CanShowRewarded();
    public bool CanShowInterstitial();
}

docs.text:

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
1. Create your ad provider:
// Example: AdMob provider
public class AdMobProvider : IAdsProvider
{
    private RewardedAd rewardedAd;
    private InterstitialAd interstitialAd;

    public AdMobProvider()
    {
        // Initialize AdMob
        MobileAds.Initialize(status => {});
        LoadAds();
    }

    public bool IsRewardedAvailable()
    {
        return rewardedAd != null && rewardedAd.IsLoaded();
    }

    public void ShowRewarded(Action onRewardGranted)
    {
        if (IsRewardedAvailable())
        {
            rewardedAd.Show();
            rewardedAd.OnUserEarnedReward += (sender, args) => {
                onRewardGranted?.Invoke();
            };
        }
    }

    // Implement other methods...
}
  1. Set provider at game start:
// In your game initialization script:
void Start()
{
    var provider = new AdMobProvider();
    AdsManager.Instance.SetProvider(provider);
}
  1. Use ads anywhere:
// Rewarded ad (player gets reward)
if (AdsManager.Instance.CanShowRewarded())
{
    AdsManager.Instance.ShowRewarded(() => {
        // Give player reward
        GiveExtraLives();
    });
}

// Interstitial ad (no reward)
if (AdsManager.Instance.CanShowInterstitial())
{
    AdsManager.Instance.ShowInterstitial();
}

docs.title: Interstitial Ads
docs.text:
Good times to show: - ✅ After game over - ✅ Every N games (e.g., every 3rd) - ✅ When returning to menu - ✅ Level transitions

Example:

int gamesPlayed = 0;

void OnGameOver()
{
    gamesPlayed++;

    if (gamesPlayed % 3 == 0)  // Every 3 games
    {
        if (AdsManager.Instance.CanShowInterstitial())
        {
            AdsManager.Instance.ShowInterstitial();
        }
    }
}

docs.text:
Offer rewards for watching: - 🎁 Extra lives/continues - 💰 Bonus points - 🔄 Undo last move - 💎 In-game currency

Example:

public void OnContinueButtonPressed()
{
    if (AdsManager.Instance.CanShowRewarded())
    {
        AdsManager.Instance.ShowRewarded(() => {
            // Reward granted!
            ContinueGame();
            ShowMessage("Continue granted!");
        });
    }
    else
    {
        ShowMessage("Ad not available");

docs.title: AdMob Integration
docs.text:
public class AdMobProvider : IAdsProvider
{
    private string rewardedId = "ca-app-pub-xxx/xxx";
    private string interstitialId = "ca-app-pub-xxx/xxx";

    private RewardedAd rewarded;
    private InterstitialAd interstitial;

    public AdMobProvider()
    {
        MobileAds.Initialize(status => {
            LoadRewardedAd();
            LoadInterstitialAd();
        });
    }

    private void LoadRewardedAd()
    {
        rewarded = new RewardedAd(rewardedId);
        AdRequest request = new AdRequest.Builder().Build();
        rewarded.LoadAd(request);
    }

    private void LoadInterstitialAd()
    {
        interstitial = new InterstitialAd(interstitialId);
        AdRequest request = new AdRequest.Builder().Build();
        interstitial.LoadAd(request);
    }

    public bool IsRewardedAvailable() 
        => rewarded != null && rewarded.IsLoaded();

    public bool IsInterstitialAvailable() 
        => interstitial != null && interstitial.IsLoaded();

    public void ShowRewarded(Action onRewardGranted)
    {
        if (IsRewardedAvailable())
        {
            rewarded.OnUserEarnedReward += (s, e) => {
                onRewardGranted?.Invoke();
                LoadRewardedAd();  // Load next
            };
            rewarded.Show();
        }
    }

    public void ShowInterstitial()
    {
        if (IsInterstitialAvailable())
        {
            interstitial.OnAdClosed += (s, e) => {
                LoadInterstitialAd();  // Load next
            };
            interstitial.Show();
        }
    }
}

    public UnityAdsProvider()
    {

    }

        => Advertisement.IsReady(rewardedPlacement);

    public bool IsInterstitialAvailable()
        => Advertisement.IsReady(interstitialPlacement);

    public void ShowRewarded(Action onRewardGranted)
    {
        rewardCallback = onRewardGranted;
        Advertisement.Show(rewardedPlacement);
    }

    public void ShowInterstitial()
    {
        Advertisement.Show(interstitialPlacement);
    }

    public void OnUnityAdsDidFinish(string placementId, ShowResult result)
    {
        if (placementId == rewardedPlacement && 
            result == ShowResult.Finished)
        {
            rewardCallback?.Invoke();
        }
    }

public class AdFrequencyManager
{
    private float lastAdTime;
    private const float MIN_TIME_BETWEEN = 180f;  // 3 minutes

    public bool CanShowAd()
    {
        float timeSince = Time.time - lastAdTime;
        return timeSince >= MIN_TIME_BETWEEN;
    }

    public void OnAdShown()
    {
        lastAdTime = Time.time;
    }
}

Turn 3: Clear 1 line again

Turn 4: Don't clear any lines

public int CalculatePotentialScore(ShapeData shape, int row, int col)
{
    int shapePoints = shape.GetCellCount();
    int potentialLines = Matrix.CountPotentialLines(shape, row, col);
    int linePoints = potentialLines × lineClearBase;
    float multiplier = GetCurrentMultiplier();

    return (int)((shapePoints + linePoints) * multiplier);
}

private AudioSource[] sfxPool;

void Awake()
{
    sfxPool = new AudioSource[5];
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++)
    {
        GameObject obj = new GameObject($"SFX_{i}");
        obj.transform.parent = transform;
        sfxPool[i] = obj.AddComponent<AudioSource>();
    }
}

public void PlaySFX(AudioClip clip)
{
    AudioSource available = Array.Find(sfxPool, s => !s.isPlaying);
    if (available != null)
    {
        available.PlayOneShot(clip);
    }
}

docs.title: Fade In/Out
docs.text:
public void FadeOutMusic(float duration)
{
    StartCoroutine(FadeOutCoroutine(duration));
}

IEnumerator FadeOutCoroutine(float duration)
{
    float startVolume = musicSource.volume;
    float elapsed = 0f;

    while (elapsed < duration)
    {
        elapsed += Time.deltaTime;
        musicSource.volume = Mathf.Lerp(startVolume, 0f, elapsed / duration);
        yield return null;
    }

    musicSource.Stop();
    musicSource.volume = startVolume;
}
